versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: GIST is staged with site-aware 8th-edition TNM (gastric vs small intestinal) layered on mitotic-rate risk stratification (Miettinen/AFIP and modified NIH criteria). T is size-based (2, 5 and 10 cm cutoffs) and identical across sites, but a small-bowel GIST of the same size and mitotic rate carries substantially higher risk than a gastric one, so primary site and mitotic index (5 or fewer vs more than 5 mitoses per 5 sq mm, formerly per 50 HPF) determine adjuvant imatinib decisions. Nodal metastasis is rare; tumour rupture upstages prognosis to high risk regardless of size.

t.label: Tumour 2 cm or smaller in greatest dimension
Tumour larger than 2 cm up to 5 cm in greatest dimension
Tumour larger than 5 cm up to 10 cm in greatest dimension
Tumour larger than 10 cm in greatest dimension

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
No regional lymph node metastasis (the usual case)
Regional lymph node metastasis (rare; seen with SDH-deficient and paediatric-type GIST)

m.label: Distant metastasis (liver and peritoneum most common; lung/bone rare)

stageGroups.basis: Gastric, low mitotic rate: very low/low risk
Gastric intermediate risk (size 5-10 cm, low mitoses)
Gastric high risk by size; small-bowel T3-T4 upstaged by site
Distant metastasis; tumour rupture behaves as high risk

versions.regionalNodes: Perigastric, periduodenal, mesenteric and omental nodes draining the primary site; nodal sampling is not routine because spread is haematogenous/peritoneal. Distant peritoneal and hepatic deposits are M1.
versions.histologicGrade: Mitotic index, not classic G1-G3: 5 or fewer vs more than 5 mitoses per 5 sq mm (reported alongside total area counted). Tumour rupture (spontaneous or intraoperative) is recorded as an independent high-risk event.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Spindle-cell (most common), epithelioid (often PDGFRA-mutant or SDH-deficient), and mixed subtypes. Molecular: KIT exon 11/9, PDGFRA (including D842V), SDH-deficient (including Carney triad/Carney-Stratakis), NF1-associated, BRAF-mutant, NTRK-rearranged.
prognosticFactors: Primary site (gastric favourable vs small bowel/rectal higher risk)
Mitotic index (5 per 5 sq mm cutoff)
KIT vs PDGFRA D842V vs SDH-deficient genotype (imatinib sensitivity)
Margin status and completeness of resection
